sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **18 of the official questions in Rhetorical Synthesis are this one** — 2 Easy, 7 Medium, 9 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The goal says 'make a generalization about' a category or 'provide an example of' something.
- The notes mix a category-level definition or statement with one or more specific instances.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Decide which level the goal wants.
- A generalization is a claim about the whole category with no single instance as its subject.
- An example is one named instance tied to the category.
- 2) For a generalization, pick the choice that makes a broad claim, often using 'most', 'all', or the plural category noun.
- For an example, pick the choice that names a specific item AND links it to the property in the goal, even if the notes use another name for that property.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The trap is the wrong level.
For a generalization, the trap lists specific instances or compares two of them.
For an example, the trap is a general category statement with no specific instance named.
Example questions also often switch terminology, where the goal uses a synonym that appears in only one note, so a choice can seem to miss the property when it actually has it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The trap is the wrong level.
For a generalization, the trap lists specific instances or compares two of them.
